text: dsh-image-skin（DSH 网页插件）：用自选图片作为 DSH 背景，并按图片配色调整界面主题。插件在网页端注册“皮肤”设置区，通过主题 token 覆盖和背景 CSS 应用图片；支持图片预览、背景透明度、填充方式、可读性遮罩及跟随图片明暗切换主题。图片缩放并提取平均色、主色和亮度，设置会保存在浏览器中并在刷新后恢复。适合希望个性化 DSH 网页外观的用户；无需 API 密钥或外部账号。

dsh-image-skin adds an image background to DSH web and adapts theme colors to the image. Its settings provide image preview, opacity and fit controls, a readability scrim, and optional automatic light or dark mode. It saves the resized image and options in browser storage. No API key is needed.
想给 DSH 网页换一张自定义背景图。
能根据背景图片自动调整页面文字和主题颜色吗？
我希望设置背景图后深色和浅色模式都能协调显示。
如何调整网页背景图片的透明度和填充方式？
想给背景图加一层遮罩，让界面内容更容易看清。
让 DSH 根据图片明暗自动切换浅色或深色主题。
I want to personalize my DSH web interface with a background picture.
Can the page colors adapt automatically to the image I choose?
dsh-image-skin 的功能「图片背景」：选择图片后将其缩放为 JPEG，并用作 DSH 网页背景。可在设置页预览、移除图片并调整铺满、适应或拉伸方式。
dsh-image-skin 的功能「配色适配」：从图片提取平均色和主色，生成浅色与深色两套界面主题 token，覆盖背景、文字、品牌色、边框及控件颜色。
dsh-image-skin 的功能「自动明暗」：开启跟随图片后，根据图片平均亮度选择浅色或深色方案；关闭或移除皮肤时恢复之前的主题偏好。
dsh-image-skin 的功能「皮肤设置」：在 DSH 设置中提供图片选择、预览、背景透明度、填充方式、遮罩和移除控件，并随界面语言显示中英文。
dsh-image-skin 的功能「刷新后恢复」：把压缩后的图片和显示选项写入浏览器 localStorage，重新打开页面时重新应用；移除皮肤会清除保存状态。

A DeepSeek Harness web plugin: set a background image and adapt the UI's text,
background, brand and border colors to the image palette automatically.

> Built with [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness).

|  |  |

dsh-image-skin README · Features：- **Background image** — pick any image (auto-downscaled to a 1600px JPEG for storage).
- **Palette adaptation** — extracts the image's average + dominant colors and
  derives a full set of `--dsw-alias-*` / `--dsw-specific-*` theme tokens
  (background surfaces, primary/secondary/tertiary labels, brand, borders,
  buttons, code blocks, the sidebar) in **both light and dark** modes,
  respecting your existing light/dark preference.
- **Contrast guarantee** — derived text colors are checked against their surface
  with WCAG relative luminance (primary/secondary ≥ 4.5:1, tertiary/caption ≥
  3:1) and nudged darker/lighter when short.
- **Opacity slider** — controls the main surface opacity; layered surfaces
  (menus/popovers/sidebar) only ease slightly and stay ≥ 80% opaque.
- **Image fit** — cover / contain / stretch.
- **Scrim** — a hue-tinted white/black veil over the image for readability on
  busy pictures.
- **Auto light/dark** — optional "follow image" switch: bright images get the
  light scheme, dark images the dark scheme; disabling it or removing the skin
  restores your previous light/dark/system preference (via a registered
  empty-token

dsh-image-skin README · How it works：Everything goes through two official seams — no DOM-structure surgery and no
hard-coded product selectors:

dsh-image-skin README · How it works：1. **`ctx.theme.overrideTokens(source, tokens)`** stacks a token layer over the
   active theme (`{ '--dsw-alias-xxx': { light, dark } }`). The theme presenter
   writes those tokens as inline CSS variables on `<body>`, so the whole app
   recolors. Removing the skin calls the returned disposer to restore the theme.
2. **One injected static CSS rule** — `body { background-image: … }`. The image
   URL, fit and scrim ride custom tokens (`--dsh-skin-bg-*`), so the theme layer
   owns them and tears them down with the layer.
3. **`ctx.theme.register` + `ctx.theme.setTheme` (auto light/dark)** — with
   "follow image" on, a scheme-carrier theme (`colorScheme: light|dark`, empty
   tokens) is registered and made active; the real colors still come from the
   override layer. Only the built-in `light/dark/system` preferences are
   persisted, so the in-process auto id never overwrites your durable preference,
   and leaving auto restores the prior one.

dsh-image-skin README · Compatible DSH versions：DSH checks a bundle's declared `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` `peerDependencies` against its own
runtime version before loading it, so check out the tag that matches the DSH you run:

| Tag | DSH runtime | `slots` service comes from |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `v1.1.0` | `0.2.0-rc.2` (0.2.x) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-renderer` |
| `v1.0.0` | `0.1.0-rc.6` (0.1.x) | `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime` |

```sh
git checkout v1.1.0    # for dsh 0.2.x
git checkout v1.0.0    # for dsh 0.1.x
```

dsh-image-skin README · Compatible DSH versions：Switching tags needs no rebuild: they differ only in the manifest
(`peerDependencies`, `dsh.client.inject`, version) and in type-erased sources, so the
emitted `lib/` bundle is the same. For development, run `pnpm install` after switching —
`pnpm-lock.yaml` is kept per tag.

dsh-image-skin README · Compatible DSH versions：These `git checkout` steps apply to a **local clone mounted with `link:`**. There is no
in-place "switch version" in `dsh plugin`: it forwards its arguments to pnpm, so changing
the installed version means changing the dependency spec (`pnpm add <spec>` inside the
profile, or `remove` + `add`). The profile then restarts on the new copy; a git spec is
compatibility-checked only after pnpm runs, and an incompatible tag is rejected and rolled
back (see below).

dsh-image-skin README · Compatible DSH versions：> A `github:` install builds itself: `package.json` declares `prepare: pnpm build`, and
> pnpm runs `prepare` on a fetched git dependency. pnpm 11 blocks that script until the
> package is allowlisted, so the first attempt fails on purpose and prints the exact key
> to add (see "Install from GitHub" below). Use the `link:` flow for development.

dsh-image-skin README · Compatible DSH versions：If the DSH log says `skipping profile bundle "dsh-image-skin"`, the checked-out tag does
not match the running runtime: switch tags rather than granting the
`dsh plugin allow-version` exemption.

dsh-image-skin README · Install into your web profile：**Local development (link, recommended)**

```sh
cd <this repo>
pnpm install && pnpm build

dsh-image-skin README · one step: install AND auto-mount (no manual file edits)：dsh plugin --profile web add link:<absolute path to this repo>
```

Then restart DSH and hard-refresh the browser (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+R). `dsh plugin`
detects `dsh.bundle.patch` and appends the package to `dsh.profile.bundles`

dsh-image-skin README · 'dsh-image-skin@github:YouHui1/dsh-image-skin#<sha>': true：dsh plugin --profile web add github:YouHui1/dsh-image-skin#v1.1.0
```

The key must match what pnpm printed, **including the commit SHA**: pnpm resolves the tag
to a commit, and a repo-level key such as `github:YouHui1/dsh-image-skin` does not match.
A different tag, or a moved tag, means a different SHA, pnpm prints a new key, and step 1
is repeated. `prepare` itself runs `pnpm build`, so the machine doing the install needs
Node ≥ 22.13 and registry access for the devDependencies.

dsh-image-skin README · 'dsh-image-skin@github:YouHui1/dsh-image-skin#<sha>': true：This repo is not published to npm (`package.json` has `"private": true`) — local
use just needs the link flow above. See `AGENTS.md` if you ever want to publish.

> Never mount through both channels at once (that loads two copies). Remove any
> leftover hand-written `insert` line from `cordis.patch.yml` before switching to
> the bundle channel.

dsh-image-skin README · Uninstall：**Bundle channel (`dsh plugin add`)**

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-image-skin
```

This removes the dependency, uninstalls the package, and drops it from
`dsh.profile.bundles`. Restart DSH + hard-refresh.

**Manual link install**: delete the `dsh-image-skin` dependency from
`~/.dsh/profiles/web/package.json`, delete the `image-skin` `insert` block from
`cordis.patch.yml`, then `pnpm install` and restart.

dsh-image-skin README · Uninstall：**Skin data**: the image lives under the `dsh-image-skin.v1` localStorage key —
tap "Remove skin" before uninstalling, or delete the key in DevTools →
Application → Local Storage.

dsh-image-skin README · Notes：- **Client-half changes** only need a hard refresh; **host-half changes** (this
  plugin's host is empty) need a DSH restart.
- Images are stored as `data:image/jpeg` (a few hundred KB), well under the
  localStorage quota.

dsh-image-skin README · Known limitations：- Very high-saturation images could tint surfaces strongly; background
  saturation is capped (`sat ≤ 45`), and layered surfaces (menus/popovers) stay
  ≥ 80% opaque to preserve readability.
